exercises.en: On weekends I sometimes cook at home, too.
exercises.why: Stem + 기 makes a noun, then 도 하다 adds 'also/sometimes'.

exercises.ko: 그 소설은 길기도 하고 어렵___ 했어요.
exercises.en: That novel was both long and difficult.
exercises.why: Both halves of the pattern need 기도: 길기도 하고 어렵기도 하다.

exercises.ko: 저는 아침에 차를 마시기도 하고 커피를 ___.
exercises.en: In the morning I drink tea and sometimes coffee.
exercises.why: The second part ends the sentence, so ~기도 해요.

exercises.ko: 제 형은 화학을 가르치기도 ___ 책을 쓰기도 해요.
exercises.en: My older brother both teaches chemistry and writes books.
exercises.why: The first ~기도 clause links to the second with 하고.

exercises.en: That person can be annoying sometimes.
exercises.why: Add 기도 straight to the stem 밉; the ㅂ irregular change only happens before a vowel.

exercises.en: When the water boils, I sometimes sprinkle in salt too.
exercises.why: ~기도 하다 attaches to the plain stem 뿌리.

exercises.ko: 혼자 사는 것은 편하기도 하고 ___ 해요.
exercises.en: Living alone is both comfortable and hard.
exercises.why: The ㄹ of 힘들다 stays before 기.

exercises.ko: 어제는 비가 오기도 하고 눈이 오기도 ___.
exercises.en: Yesterday it both rained and snowed.
exercises.why: Tense goes on the final 하다; 어제 needs past 했어요.

exercises.en: I sometimes go to the park alone.
exercises.ko: 저는 가끔 혼자 공원에 가기도 해요.

exercises.en: That bag is both cheap and pretty.
exercises.ko: 그 가방은 싸기도 하고 예쁘기도 해요.

exercises.en: On weekends I clean my room and also meet friends.
exercises.ko: 주말에는 방을 청소하기도 하고 친구를 만나기도 해요.

exercises.en: I sometimes boil ramen at night.

reading.ko: 저는 대학생이에요. 저는 한국어를 배우기도 하고 화학을 공부하기도 해요. 수업은 재미있기도 하고 어렵기도 해요. 주말에는 도서관에 가기도 하고 집에서 쉬기도 해요. 가끔 친구들과 한국어로 대화를 하기도 해요. 저는 요리를 잘 못해요. 그래서 밤에는 라면을 끓이기도 해요.
reading.en: I am a university student. I learn Korean and also study chemistry. Classes are both fun and difficult. On weekends I sometimes go to the library and sometimes rest at home. Sometimes I also have conversations with friends in Korean. I'm not good at cooking. So at night I sometimes boil ramen.

questions.a: 도서관에 가기도 하고 집에서 쉬기도 해요.

exercises.en: My friend said he is going to Busan tomorrow.
exercises.why: 가 ends in a vowel, so present-tense quoting adds ㄴ다고; 내일 rules out the past.

exercises.en: Minsu said he eats breakfast every day.
exercises.why: A verb stem ending in a consonant takes 는다고.

exercises.en: My younger sibling said these shoes are too tiny.
exercises.why: Adjectives in the present just add 다고 to the stem.

exercises.en: That person said he is a novelist.
exercises.why: A noun + 이다 is quoted with (이)라고; 소설가 ends in a vowel, so 라고.

exercises.ko: 친구가 이 가방이 자기 것이 ___ 했어요.
exercises.en: My friend said this bag isn't hers.
exercises.why: 아니다 is quoted as 아니라고, like 이다.

exercises.en: I think that novel is very interesting.
exercises.why: 재미있다 is an adjective, so the quote is just stem + 다고 before 생각하다.

exercises.en: People call that man a 'big eater'.
exercises.why: 부르다 'to call' uses (이)라고; 식신 ends in a consonant, so 이라고.

exercises.en: I heard a rumor that the singer got married.
exercises.why: Before a noun like 소문, the quote ends in 다는 (short for 다고 하는).

exercises.en: My friend said she is busy today.
Minsu said he planted a tree yesterday.
What did the teacher say?
I promised my friend I would come early tomorrow.

reading.ko: 어제 친구 지민이를 만났어요. 지민이는 요즘 소설을 쓴다고 했어요. 소설의 주인공은 작은 개라고 했어요. 저는 그 이야기가 재미있다고 생각했어요. 지민이는 다음 달에 소설을 다 쓸 거라고 했어요. 그리고 저에게 제일 먼저 보여 주겠다고 약속했어요.
reading.en: Yesterday I met my friend Jimin. Jimin said she is writing a novel these days. She said the main character of the novel is a small dog. I thought that story was interesting. Jimin said she will finish writing the novel next month. And she promised to show it to me first.

questions.q: 지민이는 언제 소설을 다 쓸 거라고 했어요?
questions.a: 다음 달에 다 쓸 거라고 했어요.

exercises.en: My friend suggested we walk together in the park.
exercises.why: ~자고 goes straight onto the stem; 걷다 only changes before a vowel.

exercises.en: My younger sibling suggested we eat ramen for dinner.
exercises.why: Suggestions are quoted with stem + 자고, with no 으 after a consonant.

exercises.en: My friend asked me if I had eaten lunch.
exercises.why: A reported question takes 냐고, here after the past 먹었.

exercises.en: That person asked me where I live.
exercises.why: The ㄹ of 살다 drops before ㄴ, so 사냐고.

exercises.en: The hotel employee asked if the room was comfortable.
exercises.why: A quoted question with an adjective ends in 냐고 before 물어보다.

exercises.ko: 가게 주인이 저에게 한국 사람___ 물어봤어요.
exercises.en: The shop owner asked me if I was Korean.
exercises.why: A question with 이다 is quoted as (이)냐고; 사람 ends in a consonant, so 이냐고.

exercises.en: My friend asked me who that gentleman was.
exercises.why: 누구 ends in a vowel, so 이다 shrinks to 냐고.

exercises.en: The lady said, "Thank you."
exercises.why: A direct quote in quotation marks always takes 라고, whatever it ends in.

exercises.en: My friend suggested we drink coffee.
Mom asked me if I was cold.
The child said, "I'm sorry."
My older sister asked me where I went yesterday.
exercises.ko: 언니가 저에게 어제 어디에 갔냐고 물어봤어요.

reading.ko: 어제 제 친구 민수가 저에게 전화했어요. 민수는 저에게 요즘 바쁘냐고 물어봤어요. 저는 조금 바쁘다고 했어요. 민수는 주말에 같이 영화를 보자고 했어요. 저는 무슨 영화냐고 물어봤어요. 민수는 "슬픈 영화야"라고 말했어요. 저는 슬픈 영화를 싫어해요. 그래서 다른 영화를 보자고 했어요.
reading.en: Yesterday my friend Minsu called me. Minsu asked me if I was busy these days. I said I was a little busy. Minsu suggested we watch a movie together on the weekend. I asked what movie it was. Minsu said, "It's a sad movie." I don't like sad movies. So I suggested we watch a different movie.

questions.q: 저는 왜 다른 영화를 보자고 했어요?

exercises.en: The teacher told the students to watch a Korean movie.
exercises.why: Commands are quoted with (으)라고; 보 ends in a vowel, so 라고.

exercises.en: The doctor told me to take the medicine.
exercises.why: 먹 ends in a consonant, so the command quote is 으라고.

exercises.en: Mom told me to renew my passport.
exercises.why: 하다 verbs end in a vowel, so the command quote is 하라고.

exercises.ko: 친구가 저에게 그 영화를 ___ 말라고 했어요.
exercises.en: My friend told me not to watch that movie.
exercises.why: A quoted 'don't' is stem + 지 말라고.

exercises.en: Dad told me not to talk rudely.
exercises.why: The negative command quote uses 말다 → 말라고; the ㄹ stays.

exercises.en: My native-speaker friend told me to use honorific speech.
exercises.why: 쓰 ends in a vowel, so the command quote is 쓰라고.

exercises.en: The teacher told the students to run fast.
exercises.why: Add 라고 directly to the vowel stem 뛰.

exercises.ko: 엄마가 동생___ 음식을 흘리지 말라고 하셨어요.
exercises.en: Mom told my younger sibling not to spill food.
exercises.why: The person who gets the order is marked with 에게.

exercises.en: My friend told me to come quickly.
The teacher told us not to exaggerate.
Mom told me to clean my room.
The doctor told me not to eat spicy food.
exercises.ko: 의사 선생님이 저에게 매운 음식을 먹지 말라고 하셨어요.

reading.ko: 지난주에 저는 식중독에 걸렸어요. 밤에 배가 아파서 토했어요. 다음 날 병원에 갔어요. 의사 선생님이 저에게 물을 많이 마시라고 하셨어요. 그리고 매운 음식을 먹지 말라고 하셨어요. 엄마는 저에게 집에서 쉬라고 하셨어요. 그래서 저는 학교에 가지 않고 집에서 쉬었어요.
reading.en: Last week I got food poisoning. At night my stomach hurt, so I threw up. The next day I went to the hospital. The doctor told me to drink a lot of water. And he told me not to eat spicy food. Mom told me to rest at home. So I didn't go to school and rested at home.

questions.a: 물을 많이 마시라고 하셨어요. 그리고 매운 음식을 먹지 말라고 하셨어요.

exercises.en: My friend asked me to give him a pen.
exercises.why: The speaker wanted it for himself, so 주다 becomes 달라고.

exercises.ko: 동생이 저에게 신발 끈을 ___ 달라고 했어요.
exercises.en: My younger sibling asked me to tie his shoelaces.
exercises.why: A favor for the speaker is ~아/어 달라고: 묶어 달라고.

exercises.en: My older sister told me to give food to the cat.
exercises.why: The cat, not my sister, gets the food, so the normal command quote 주라고.

exercises.en: The customer asked the employee to take a photo for her.
exercises.why: ~아/어 달라고 reports a request to do something for the speaker.

exercises.en: I asked my friend to help me with my homework.
exercises.why: 부탁하다 is the verb 'to ask a favor' and often follows 달라고.

exercises.en: I told my friend I had a favor to ask.
exercises.why: 부탁 is the subject of 있다 and ends in a consonant, so 이.

exercises.en: The teacher told me to help Minsu.
exercises.why: Minsu gets the help, not the teacher, so 도와주라고.

exercises.en: The new employee asked me to teach him the work.
exercises.why: 가르치다 + 어 contracts to 가르쳐 before 달라고.

exercises.en: My friend asked me to buy him coffee.
exercises.ko: 친구가 저에게 커피를 사 달라고 했어요.

exercises.en: Mom told me to give this book to my younger sibling.
exercises.ko: 엄마가 저에게 이 책을 동생에게 주라고 하셨어요.

exercises.en: I asked my older brother to tie the string.
The customer asked for water.

reading.ko: 우리 회사에 신입사원이 왔어요. 그 사원의 이름은 지훈이에요. 지훈 씨는 일을 잘하려고 애써요. 어제 지훈 씨가 저에게 설문조사를 도와 달라고 부탁했어요. 그런데 저는 너무 바빴어요. 그래서 부장님이 그 일을 민수 씨에게 주라고 하셨어요. 민수 씨가 지훈 씨를 도와줬어요.
reading.en: A new employee came to our company. His name is Jihun. Jihun tries hard to do his work well. Yesterday Jihun asked me to help him with a survey. But I was too busy. So the manager told me to give that job to Minsu. Minsu helped Jihun.

questions.a: 그 일을 민수 씨에게 주라고 하셨어요.

exercises.en: Dad made me exercise every day.
exercises.why: Stem + 게 하다 means 'make/let someone do'.

exercises.en: That movie made me cry.
exercises.why: The ㄹ of 울다 stays before 게.

exercises.ko: 동생이 깨지 않___ 작게 말해 주세요.
exercises.en: Please speak softly so my younger sibling doesn't wake up.
exercises.why: ~지 않게 + verb means 'so that ... not'.

exercises.ko: 다른 사람들이 볼 수 있___ 목록을 문에 붙였어요.
exercises.en: I put the list on the door so other people could see it.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ 수 있게 + verb means 'so that someone can'.

exercises.en: My older sister had me put on that ring.
exercises.why: 게 attaches to the plain stem 끼, with no 어.

exercises.ko: 엄마가 저를 혼자 축제에 못 ___ 하셨어요.
exercises.en: Mom didn't let me go to the festival alone.
exercises.why: 못 ~게 하다 means 'not let someone do'.

exercises.en: This music makes people happy.
exercises.why: Adjective stem + 게 하다 means 'make someone feel/be that way'.

exercises.en: Wear warm clothes so you don't catch a cold.
exercises.why: ~지 않게 gives the purpose: 'so that ... not'.

exercises.en: My friend made me laugh.
The teacher let us go home early.
exercises.ko: 선생님이 우리를 일찍 집에 가게 하셨어요.

exercises.en: I'll make a list so I don't forget.
That news made my mom sad.

reading.ko: 지난 주말에 우리 동네에서 축제가 있었어요. 엄마는 저와 동생을 축제에 가게 하셨어요. 축제에는 상점이 많았어요. 우리는 상점들을 천천히 둘러봤어요. 동생이 길을 잃지 않게 저는 동생의 손을 꼭 잡았어요. 동생은 과자를 하나 샀어요. 그 축제는 우리를 아주 즐겁게 했어요.
reading.en: Last weekend there was a festival in our neighborhood. Mom let my younger sibling and me go to the festival. There were many stores at the festival. We slowly looked around the stores. I held my sibling's hand tightly so he wouldn't get lost. My sibling bought a snack. The festival made us very happy.

exercises.en: The teacher makes the students exercise every day.
exercises.why: Swap 하다 for 시키다 to make someone else do it.

exercises.en: That match got people excited.
exercises.why: With an object (사람들을), use 흥분시키다 'to excite someone'.

exercises.en: Shall we order pizza for dinner?
exercises.why: 시키다 means 'to order food'; 시키 + ㄹ까요.

exercises.en: The manager gives the new employee a lot of work.
exercises.why: The person given the task takes 에게.

exercises.en: The doctor stabilized the patient first.
exercises.why: 안정하다 → 안정시키다 'to make someone stable'.

exercises.en: The teacher reminded the students of the exam date.
exercises.why: 상기시키다 'to remind' makes someone else recall something.

exercises.en: My older brother and I fought. Mom got us to make up.
exercises.why: Mom made us make up, so 화해시키다.

exercises.ko: 음식을 너무 많이 ___ 다 못 먹었어요.
exercises.en: We ordered too much food, so we couldn't eat it all.
exercises.why: 시키 + 어서 contracts to 시켜서; tense is not marked before 아/어서.

exercises.en: We ordered two coffees.
Dad sent my younger brother on an errand.
The teacher makes us study hard.
Shall we order pizza right now?

reading.ko: 오늘은 토요일이에요. 아침에 엄마가 저에게 심부름을 시키셨어요. 저는 가게에서 우유와 빵을 샀어요. 집에 와서 동생을 공부시켰어요. 동생은 공부를 싫어해요. 그래서 공부가 끝난 후에 동생을 마음껏 놀게 했어요. 저녁에는 가족들과 피자를 시켰어요. 피자는 아주 맛있었어요.
reading.en: Today is Saturday. In the morning Mom sent me on an errand. I bought milk and bread at the store. When I came home, I made my younger sibling study. My sibling hates studying. So after studying was over, I let him play as much as he liked. In the evening we ordered pizza with the family. The pizza was very tasty.

exercises.en: For lunch I eat gimbap or ramen.
exercises.why: 김밥 ends in a consonant, so 'or' is 이나.

exercises.en: On weekends I hang out with a friend or my younger sibling.
exercises.why: 친구 ends in a vowel, so 나.

exercises.en: In the evening I read a book or watch TV.
exercises.why: Between two actions, 'or' is stem + 거나.

exercises.en: If it's cold or it rains, I exercise at home.
exercises.why: 거나 starts with a consonant, so 춥다 keeps its ㅂ.

exercises.ko: 오늘은 할 일이 없어요. 집에서 영화___ 볼까요?
exercises.en: There's nothing to do today. Shall we just watch a movie at home?
exercises.why: One noun + (이)나 means 'just ... I guess'; 영화 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: There's no juice. I guess I'll just drink water.
exercises.why: 물 ends in a consonant, so the 'settling' form is 이나.

exercises.en: I'll go by bus or subway.
exercises.why: With (이)나, the particle 로 appears only after the second noun.

exercises.en: I'll do my homework or clean the house.
exercises.why: 하다 is a verb, so 'or' is 거나, not (이)나.

exercises.en: Shall we meet on Saturday or Sunday?
After school I go to the gym or the library.
When I have worries, I talk with a friend or walk alone.
exercises.ko: 고민이 있으면 친구와 이야기하거나 혼자 걸어요.

exercises.en: Let's just eat at home today.

reading.ko: 다음 주에 중간고사가 있어요. 그래서 요즘 저는 도서관에서 공부하거나 친구들과 같이 공부해요. 저녁에는 김밥이나 라면을 먹어요. 시간이 없어서 요리를 못 해요. 오늘은 너무 피곤해요. 그래서 오늘 밤에는 공부하지 않고 잠이나 자야겠어요. 시험이 끝나면 영화를 보거나 여행할 거예요.
reading.en: Next week I have midterm exams. So these days I study at the library or study together with friends. In the evening I eat gimbap or ramen. I have no time, so I can't cook. Today I'm very tired. So tonight I won't study; I guess I'll just sleep. When the exams are over, I'll watch a movie or travel.
